title: Hichilema re-election expected to preserve Zambia's copper policy
gist: Hakainde Hichilema's decisive re-election as Zambia's president (declared 18 August, ~3 million votes, >1.1 million margin) is read by Benchmark as preserving policy continuity for copper, including the beneficiation agenda in Zambia's 2024 critical minerals strategy, with 2026 mined output estimated at 901kt (+11% y/y) and a government target of 3Mtpa by 2031.

insights.claim: Hakainde Hichilema was declared Zambia's president-elect on 18 August after winning nearly 3 million votes, more than 1.1 million ahead of NRPUP's Brian Mundubile and comfortably above the 50% threshold needed to avoid a run-off.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A decisive first-round win removes election-uncertainty risk premium from Zambian copper assets and signals a stable mandate.

insights.claim: Benchmark's policy analyst expects Hichilema's re-election to deliver policy and geopolitical continuity in Zambia, including continuation of the beneficiation (in-country value-add) agenda set out in the country's 2024 critical minerals strategy.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Miners and offtakers in Zambia can expect a stable regulatory framework, but should also expect continued pressure toward downstream processing rather than raw ore export.
insights.quote: The result is expected to deliver policy and geopolitical continuity, including the continuation of the beneficiation agenda set out in Zambia's 2024 critical minerals strategy

insights.claim: Copper accounts for roughly three-quarters of the total value of Zambia's exports, making national policy heavily copper-dependent.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Zambia's fiscal reliance on copper aligns government incentives with mining-sector growth, reducing expropriation/royalty-shock risk while prices support export revenue.
insights.locator: Copper is a crucial export for Zambia

insights.claim: Benchmark's Copper Service assesses Zambia's 2026 mined copper production at 901kt, an 11% increase over the prior year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Double-digit supply growth from Zambia is a marginal bearish input for copper supply-demand balances and a positive read for operators exposed to the Zambian copperbelt.

insights.claim: The Zambian government is targeting an increase in copper output to 3Mtpa by 2031, more than tripling the 2026 estimate of 901kt.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: If even partially achieved, a 3Mtpa ambition would make Zambia a top-tier copper supplier this decade; watch investment approvals and beneficiation requirements as gating factors.
